sources.title: The Urals and Western Siberia in the Bronze and Iron Ages
sources.note: Cambridge synthesis of western Siberian archaeology, interactions, metallurgy, pastoralism, and cultural change.

sources.title: Prehistoric Mongolian Archaeology in the Early 21st Century
sources.note: Peer reviewed synthesis of eastern steppe and Xiongnu archaeology, settlements, mobility, hierarchy, and evidentiary gaps.

sources.title: The establishment and dissolution of the Turk empire
sources.note: Cambridge history states that the name Turk and securely attributable Turkic text cannot be traced with certainty before the sixth century CE.

sources.title: New radiocarbon dates and a review of Minusinsk Basin chronology
sources.note: Radiocarbon study of Minusinsk sequences, including broad and uncertain Tagar and Tes phase ranges.

sources.title: Radiocarbon chronology of post-Scythian burial practices in the Minusinsk Basin
sources.note: Large new series showing diverse mortuary practices and gradual overlap rather than a clean cultural replacement.

sources.title: Current problems in the study of Tagar dwellings
sources.note: University repository study emphasizing the weak settlement sample and unresolved classification of Tagar houses.

sources.title: Iron Age pastoral nomadism and agriculture in the eastern Eurasian steppe
sources.note: Peer reviewed dental and isotope comparison of Ai-Dai in Minusinsk and Aymyrlyg in Tuva.

sources.title: Dental palaeopathology in Eneolithic to Early Iron Age Minusinsk
sources.note: University research record reporting caries, calculus, enamel hypoplasia, age, sex, and dietary interpretation.

sources.title: Radiocarbon chronology of Sargat culture sites in Western Siberia
sources.note: Russian Archaeology study of 118 contexts from settlements and cemeteries, dating and uneven sampling.

sources.title: Architectural traditions of the Trans-Urals forest-steppe in the Early Iron Age
sources.note: Peer reviewed study of Sargat dwelling types, building methods, insulation, and multi-chamber household complexes.

sources.title: Sargat burial sites in the Middle Irtysh: a gender analysis
sources.note: Siberian Branch RAS study treating bodies and burial objects together while framing gender conclusions as hypotheses.

sources.title: Woven belts from Sargat mound 7 at Chepkul-9
sources.note: Siberian Branch RAS textile study of wool and plant-fiber belts dated broadly from the third century BCE to first century CE.

sources.title: Ceramic spindle whorls from the Galechnoye-1 Sargat settlement
sources.note: Siberian Branch RAS record of textile-production tools from a western Siberian forest-steppe settlement.

sources.title: Women and children in the Sargat culture
sources.note: Scholarly chapter using varied child and adult graves to examine age, gender, status, and mortuary selection.

sources.title: Kinship analysis of human remains from Sargat mounds
sources.note: Siberian Branch RAS paleogenetic study of nine people from two Baraba forest-steppe mounds.

sources.title: Biological affinities among western Siberian forest-steppe groups
sources.note: Study of non-metric dental traits in 480 people, revealing differences among river basins and Baraba.

sources.title: New results from dwellings at the Ivolga Fortress
sources.note: Excavation report on three dwellings, burned abandonment, pottery, household objects, animal bones, and stratigraphy.

sources.title: Settlement patterns and domestic economy of the Xiongnu in Khanui Valley
sources.note: Primary settlement study on seasonal location patterns, domestic economy, mixed production, and regional variation.

sources.title: Ivolginsk Xiongnu Fortress archaeozoological research
sources.note: Published excavation study identifying diverse domestic and hunted animal taxa at Ivolga.

sources.title: Cultivating Complexity: Ivolga and its environment
sources.note: Oxford synthesis locating Ivolga among steppe, taiga, pine forest, and the Selenga River.

sources.title: Parasites provide evidence for fish consumption among Iron Age Siberian pastoralists
sources.note: Open access archaeoparasitology at Tunnug 1 showing dietary variety and infection risks from fish and animal foods.

sources.title: Iron Age Archaeology and Trauma from Aymyrlyg, South Siberia
sources.note: University-hosted monograph record integrating skeletal trauma, health, diet, occupations, and warfare at Aymyrlyg.

sources.title: Antiquities from the Pazyryk Burial Mounds
sources.note: State Hermitage catalogue documenting earlier Altai leather-cushion saddles, decorated saddle cloths, horse gear, clothing, and preservation.

sources.title: Proto-Turkic: Reconstruction Problems
sources.note: Specialist linguistic study presenting Proto-Turkic as scholarly reconstruction rather than an excavated written language.

sources.title: Radiocarbon reservoir offsets in the Cis-Baikal region
sources.note: Paired human and animal dating study showing how freshwater foods can distort chronology and reveal diet.
